name: Arba Kokalari, Michael McNamara - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689 and (EU) 2018/1139 as regards the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Digital Omnibus on AI)
part_text:
The report sets out Parliament's position on simplifying how the EU's artificial intelligence rules are applied. It postpones the start of the strictest rules for high-risk AI systems: to 2 December 2027 for systems on a list of sensitive uses, and 2 August 2028 for AI built into products like medical devices or machinery. It also adds a ban on AI that creates sexual images of real people without consent, and softens some paperwork and literacy duties.

- What changes: later deadlines for high-risk AI rules, a new ban on fake sexual images, lighter AI literacy and registration duties.
- Who it affects: companies making or using high-risk AI, small firms, and people targeted by image-abuse tools.
- What happens next: this is Parliament's first-reading position; talks with EU governments follow before it becomes law.
